description:
FILED s407 (Fable review, fable-answers-s406.md §5.2).  RULED: in eval-string
mode a #138-family drop DIES perl-shaped, so the eval returns undef with $@ set —
exactly what the ruled `PCL: unsupported in string eval:` refusals already do.

WHY: p-ensure-transpiler starts `pl2cl --server` with :error nil, so the
transpile-time announcement (Parser.pm _announce_dropped_statement) can never be
seen there — the emitter's own comment says so.  Measured:
    sub f {…} sub g {…} my $u="x";
    my $r = eval q{ f ref $u, "m" or g "fb"; 7 };    perl: f( m) g(fb) r=7
                                                    PCL : r=7, $@ "", the call GONE, nothing on stderr
    use feature 'try';
    my $r = eval q{ my $v=1; try { die "x\n" } catch ($e) { $v="c:$e" } $v };
                                                    perl: c:x     PCL: undef, $@ ""  (whole body swallowed)
perl's contract for eval STRING is "what does not compile sets $@"; the reader of
stderr does not exist here; and this is the announce->DIE step Option B phase 2
ends with (fable-answers-s400 §6.4), taken early ONLY for the path that cannot
announce.  File mode is untouched (still announce, rc 0, until phase 2).

SHAPE: at the two PARSE-ERROR emitters (Pl/Parser.pm, where
_announce_dropped_statement is called), when $self->eval_mode: die with the
fixed prefix text ("PCL: statement dropped at (eval) line N: <text> -- <reason>")
so the server returns "err" and p-eval-string sets $@.  Check that the "PCL:"
re-raise path (_shape_expr_error, ExprToCL ~1358) already carries it to $@ —
reuse it, do not add a second channel.

BAR (s373 three legs, adapted): (1) POPULATION FIRST — one instrumented sweep
(and one --quick companion) counting eval-mode drops per file BEFORE flipping
(env var that logs "file\tline\ttext" from the emitter to a path), so every
row that will move is known with its cause; (2) the flip; (3) sweep
TOTAL/LOST + companion, rows spliced with causes.  gate-set-scan not needed
(file mode unchanged).  Guard rows: the two probes above via Pl/t (perl-oracle
rows: $@ non-empty, value undef) — note the try one also needs #364 to PASS
rather than die; until then it asserts the die.


DONE s408 (Opus 5), the ruled shape, with the bar met in order.

(1) POPULATION FIRST, via a PCL_EVAL_DROP_LOG instrument in the emitter:
48 events / 34 unique statements over perl-tests, 548 / 446 over perls own t/.
The SHAPES were the finding -- most are DELIBERATELY INVALID Perl the tests eval
to assert $@ is set (`1+;`, `]`, `$foo =;`, `0x.3`, the yada forms), where perl
sets $@ and PCL returned undef with $@ EMPTY.  The valid-Perl residue is the
postfix-deref family, `<FH> // 0`, `do $subref()`.

(2) THE FLIP: _announce_dropped_statement DIES when eval_mode, before the
ANNOUNCE_DROPS gate (what that flag controls is a diagnostic, not whether a
statement may vanish) and after the collect_prototypes_only guard.  Text keeps
the `PCL:` prefix so it travels the route the ruled refusals already take.

(3) MEASURED -- and the first number was a LIE worth recording.  The first sweep
said -66 rows, -61 of them index.t ALONE.  index.t does `eval $test_str; die $@
if $@;` and its $test_str was MALFORMED -- by a separate silent-wrong this flip
EXPOSED: `qq {...}` with whitespace before the delimiter kept the delimiters in
the string value (task #375, fixed here).  With that fixed the real cost is FOUR
rows net: -3 dor.t, -2 postfixderef.t, -1 yadayada.t (each a '... compiles'
assertion about code PCL cannot lower -- passing ONLY because the failure was
silent), +1 eval.t (an invalid construct now sets $@ as perl does) and +1
magic.t (#375).  Baselines edited ROW BY ROW with causes; re-run: 0 new / 0
fixed, TOTAL 18513 = baseline, drops 12 = census.  Gate 149/5436.

METHOD NOTE for the next session: a big regression number is not a cost until
the files own mechanism is read.  -61 of -66 was one file DELIBERATELY dying on
$@, on a string another bug had corrupted.
subject: A DROP inside a string eval is SILENT (even with PCL_DROP_ANNOUNCE=all) — in eval mode a drop must DIE into $@
